summary: This short section gives the Central Government the power to make rules. These rules are meant to help carry out the purposes of this specific chapter of the law. The text provided is very brief and does not give any further details.
points: The Central Government is allowed to make rules.
The rules must be for carrying out the purposes of this Chapter.
example: The Central Government decides it needs to clarify how certain producer companies under Chapter XXI should manage their internal affairs according to the law. To make this clear for everyone, the government uses its power under Section 378ZU to officially write and release a new set of rules. Meera Textiles Private Limited, a company registered under this part of the Act, reads these new rules to ensure they are following the government guidelines properly while running their daily business operations in the market.

terms.meaning: The national government of the country.
Official instructions or guidelines created to help apply a law.

watch: Do not confuse this general rule-making power with specific rules found in other chapters of the Act.
